sections.heading: 1. What is a Tissue
points: A **tissue** = a group of **similar cells** performing a **specific function** together.
Tissues allow **division of labour** in multicellular organisms → greater efficiency.
Plants and animals have **different** kinds of tissues.

sections.heading: 2. Plant Tissues

points.text: **Permanent tissue** — cells that have stopped dividing:
sub: **Simple:** parenchyma (storage), collenchyma (flexibility), sclerenchyma (hard support — e.g. husk).

points: **Epidermis** covers plant parts; **stomata** allow gas exchange.

sections.heading: 3. Animal Tissues
points: **Epithelial tissue** — covers/lines body surfaces and organs (protection, absorption).
**Connective tissue** — binds and supports: **blood, bone, cartilage, ligaments, tendons, adipose (fat)**.

sections.heading: 4. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Tissue = group of similar cells doing a specific function (division of labour).
Plant: meristematic (dividing — apical/lateral/intercalary) vs permanent (parenchyma, collenchyma, sclerenchyma; xylem/phloem).
Xylem = water transport; phloem = food transport.
Animal tissues: epithelial, connective (blood/bone/cartilage), muscular (striated/smooth/cardiac), nervous.
Neurons = nerve cells; blood is a connective tissue.

sections.heading: 5. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Blood, bone and cartilage are connective** tissues.
**Cardiac muscle** (heart) is involuntary but striated; **skeletal/striated** muscle is voluntary.
